title: Polarization and Malus's Law
learning_goal: Investigate polarization and use Malus's Law to analyze transmitted light intensity.

stages.title: 1. Polarization
stages.content: Polarization restricts the direction in which a transverse wave oscillates. Light can be polarized because electromagnetic waves are transverse.

stages.title: 2. Malus's Law
stages.content: For polarized light passing through an analyzer, transmitted intensity is I = I₀cos²θ, where θ is the angle between the incoming polarization direction and the analyzer axis.

stages.title: 3. Special angles
stages.content: If θ = 0°, the analyzer is aligned and the transmitted intensity is maximum. If θ = 90°, ideally no light is transmitted.

stages.title: 4. Worked example
stages.content: If polarized light with intensity I₀ passes through an analyzer at 60°, then I = I₀cos²60° = 0.25I₀.

stages.title: 5. Guided practice
stages.prompt: Polarized light enters an analyzer at 45°. What fraction of the original intensity is transmitted?
stages.alternate_explanation: At 45°, the cosine-squared factor is one-half.

stages.title: 6. Mastery check
stages.content: To demonstrate mastery, explain polarization, use I = I₀cos²θ, identify maximum and minimum transmission orientations, and connect polarization to technologies such as LCDs and 3-D glasses.
